description.en-US: The stable identifier this campaign is named by in reports and imports. Immutable, because a promotion's cost is reviewed long after it ends and the reference must still resolve.
What appears on a receipt line explaining the discount, snapshotted onto the adjustment at the time of sale so renaming the campaign later does not rewrite what a customer was told.

Whether this program applies on its own when its conditions hold, or only when a customer presents a code. One engine serves both (BR 21-22 forbid separate engines for promotions and vouchers): the difference is entirely this flag plus whether a code was supplied, not two evaluation paths that could disagree.

Application order, LOWER FIRST (D-10). Ascending rather than descending because the first-applied program operates on the largest base, which is where an operator naturally wants their headline offer. Ties break by created_at then id, so the ordering is total and never depends on database record order (BR 29).

When the campaign starts, or NULL for always. Effective dating rather than archiving on a schedule, so a campaign can be set up in advance and so an order priced under a past campaign can still be explained.
When it stops, or NULL for open-ended. Exclusive of the instant itself.

How this program combines with others when no explicit compatibility row decides (D-08). exclusive means it applies alone on the order; exclusive_within_group excludes only programs sharing its exclusive_group. It is the FALLBACK, not the rule: an explicit denied row always wins, then an explicit allowed row, then this (D-09).

Names a set of programs at most one of which may apply — 'seasonal', 'staff_discount'. A free string rather than a foreign key, because a group has no properties of its own: it is nothing more than the name tying its members together.

How many times this program may be used in total, or NULL for unlimited. Enforced by a conditional UPDATE checking the affected row count rather than by a read-then-write (D-31), because two simultaneous redemptions of a last-remaining voucher must not both succeed.

How many times one customer may use it, or NULL for unlimited. Only meaningful on an order carrying a customer_reference: an anonymous sale cannot be counted against a customer, so this limit does not apply to one.

What happens to this program's discount when part of the order comes back (BR 31). preserve keeps the customer's original benefit; revalidate re-runs the engine over the remaining basket and reclaims the difference as a clawback adjustment (D-12). Defaults to preserve, the customer-favourable reading: reclaiming a discount someone already walked out with needs a deliberate business decision. Required by BR 31 and absent from the BR 22 field list.

Whether a fully returned order gives its voucher use back (BR 32). Defaults true: a customer who returned everything did not receive the benefit, and consuming their one-time voucher anyway would be taking something for nothing.

Whether a partial return gives the voucher use back (BR 32). Defaults false, unlike its full-return counterpart: the customer did keep part of the benefit, so returning the use as well would let one voucher fund two purchases.
